title: Sunrise at Mount Bromo
text:
Saturday 9 August

Dear Diary,

I am so tired, but today was one of the best days of my whole life!

We woke up at three o'clock this morning. It was pitch black and freezing cold, so I wore two jumpers, a woolly hat and Dad's gloves, which were far too big for me. A jeep took us up a steep, bumpy road to a viewpoint. Hundreds of people were already there, waiting quietly in the dark.

Slowly, the sky changed from black to purple, then pink, then gold. Below us, a sea of white cloud filled the valley, and Mount Bromo rose out of it, puffing out a grey plume of smoke. It looked like a giant sleeping dragon breathing out. My little sister Tia forgot all about the cold and just stared with her mouth open.

After sunrise, we drove across a huge plain of grey sand called the Sea of Sand. Then we climbed more than two hundred steps to the edge of the crater. My legs were burning by the time we reached the top! When I peeked over the edge, I could hear the volcano rumbling deep inside, and there was a smell like rotten eggs. Mum said it was sulphur.

I think everybody should watch the sun rise over Bromo at least once. I am going to stick my ticket into this diary so that I never forget it.

Goodnight,
Lintang
